title: UX/UI: port ember's Blocks theme, responsive layout
outcome: The dashboard page uses js/ember's 'Blocks' design system (shaped-panel/ink-shadow visual language) instead of m1's plain CSS, and is comfortably usable on a phone -- replacing m1's minimal styling without changing the underlying data-fetching logic from m1/m2.

included: Add Tailwind v4 to this repo (js/ember's Blocks theme is built on it -- @import 'tailwindcss' in globals.css, PostCSS config) -- this is a real, deliberate new dependency, not incidental; it exists because the theme requires it.

Port the relevant CSS layer primitives from js/ember/src/app/globals.css's @layer ember block (the .panel/.pink/.pf shaped-panel primitives, .kick caption styling, relevant CSS custom properties like --orange/--ink-3, font-serif) into this repo's own globals.css -- copied and import-fixed, never regenerated from scratch (js/ember's own stated convention).

Port js/ember/src/components/ui/panel.tsx (Panel, Kicker) and card.tsx (Card and its subcomponents) into this repo, adapted to not depend on anything js/ember-specific beyond the cn() utility (also portable from js/ember/src/lib/utils.ts).

Apply the ported components to the dashboard page: accounts grouped by institution rendered via Panel and/or Card instead of plain-CSS markup, preserving all of m1/m2's data-fetching, error-state, and loading behavior unchanged.
Responsive/mobile-friendly layout -- the page must be comfortably readable and usable on a phone-sized viewport, tying back to m2's actual motivation for deploying this at all.
excluded: Any change to SimpleFin fetch logic, the MCP route, or auth -- this milestone is presentation-only.
A dedicated research/IA-direction task -- the design system already exists; this is a porting/application task (see docs/product/MILESTONES.md's m3 grill notes).
New pages, navigation, or features beyond restyling the existing single dashboard page.
Porting js/ember components beyond Panel/Kicker/Card unless a task genuinely needs one more primitive -- do not import the whole component library speculatively.

behaviors.description: The dashboard page visually uses the Blocks theme's shaped-panel/ink-shadow primitives (Panel/Card) instead of m1's plain CSS, grouping accounts by institution the same way as before.
Viewed at a phone-sized viewport width, the page's content (account groups, balances) is fully readable and usable without horizontal scrolling or overlapping elements.
All of m1/m2's functional behavior is unchanged: the same data renders, the same error states (missing env var, upstream failure) still display clearly, just restyled.
